message.content:
Erlang/OTP SSH is the built-in SSH server component of the Erlang/OTP platform.

A critical vulnerability was discovered in the Erlang/OTP SSH server, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary system commands remotely without authentication by crafting specific SSH protocol messages. In `/app/workspace/otp_src_27.3.2` we provide the source code of an affected version of Erlang/OTP SSH server.

Try to investigate which type of ssh message will cause this attack, and fix this bug. After the bugfix, the server should maintain normal SSH behavior and block this type of attack. The unauthorized ssh message should not be able to execute any system commands.

Just do the fix inside the provided code. No need to build and start the Erlang/OTP server.

    75→%%                        
    76→%% Description: Handles channel messages received on the ssh-connection.
    77→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
    78→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _ConnectionHandler,
    79→		{data, _ChannelId, _Type, Data}},

   104→	    {env, ChannelId, WantReply, Var, Value}}, State = #state{encoding=Enc0}) ->
   105→    %% It is not as simple as it sounds to set environment variables
   106→    %% in the server.
   107→    %% The (OS) env vars should be per per Channel; otherwise anyone
   108→    %% could affect anyone other's variables.
   109→    %% Therefore this clause always return a failure.
   110→    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler,
   111→				 WantReply, failure, ChannelId),
   112→
   113→    %% https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/7908799/xbd/envvar.html
   114→    %% LANG
   115→    %%     This variable determines the locale category for native language,
   116→    %%     local customs and coded character set in the absence of the LC_ALL
   117→    %%     and other LC_* (LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY,
   118→    %%     LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) environment variables. This can be used by
   119→    %%     applications to determine the language to use for error messages
   120→    %%     and instructions, collating sequences, date formats, and so forth. 
   121→    %% LC_ALL
   122→    %%     This variable determines the values for all locale categories. The
   123→    %%     value of the LC_ALL environment variable has precedence over any of
   124→    %%     the other environment variables starting with LC_ (LC_COLLATE,
   125→    %%     LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) and the
   126→    %%     LANG environment variable.
   127→    %% ...
   128→    %%
   129→    %%  The values of locale categories are determined by a precedence order;
   130→    %%  the first condition met below determines the value:
   131→    %%
   132→    %%   1. If the LC_ALL environment variable is defined and is not null,
   133→    %%      the value of LC_ALL is used.
   134→    %%
   135→    %%   2. If the LC_* environment variable ( LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES,
   136→    %%      LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) is defined and is not null, the
   137→    %%      value of the environment variable is used to initialise the category
   138→    %%      that corresponds to the environment variable.
   139→    %%
   140→    %%   3. If the LANG environment variable is defined and is not null, the value
   141→    %%      of the LANG environment variable is used.
   142→    %%
   143→    %%   4. If the LANG environment variable is not set or is set to the empty string,
   144→    %%      the implementation-dependent default locale is used.

   148→        %% arrives in different messages and in an undefined order, it is resolved
   149→        %% like this:

   171→    Pty = Pty0#ssh_pty{width = Width, height = Height,
   172→		       pixel_width = PixWidth,
   173→		       pixel_height = PixHeight},
   174→    {Chars, NewBuf} = io_request({window_change, Pty0}, Buf, Pty, undefined),
   175→    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Chars),
   176→    {ok, State#state{pty = Pty, buf = NewBuf}};
   177→
   178→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,  {shell, ChannelId, WantReply}}, #state{shell=disabled} = State) ->
   179→    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, 1, "Prohibited."),
   180→    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
   181→    ssh_connection:exit_status(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS),
   182→    ssh_connection:send_eof(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId),
   183→    {stop, ChannelId, State#state{channel = ChannelId, cm = ConnectionHandler}};
   184→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,  {shell, ChannelId, WantReply}}, State0) ->
   185→    State = case State0#state.encoding of
   186→                undefined -> State0#state{encoding = utf8};
   187→                _-> State0
   188→            end,
   189→    NewState = start_shell(ConnectionHandler, State),
   190→    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
   191→    {ok, NewState#state{channel = ChannelId,
   192→			cm = ConnectionHandler}};
   193→
   194→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,  {exec, ChannelId, WantReply, Cmd0}}, S0) ->
   195→    {Enc,S1} = guess_encoding(Cmd0, S0),
   196→    Cmd = unicode:characters_to_list(Cmd0, Enc),
   197→    case
   198→        case S1#state.exec of
   199→            disabled ->
   200→                {"Prohibited.", ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS, 1};
   201→
   202→            {direct,F} ->
   203→                %% Exec called and a Fun or MFA is defined to use.  The F returns the
   204→                %% value to return.
   205→                %% The standard I/O is directed from/to the channel ChannelId.
   206→                exec_direct(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, F, WantReply, S1);
   207→
   208→            undefined when S0#state.shell == ?DEFAULT_SHELL ; 
   209→                           S0#state.shell == disabled ->
   210→                %% Exec called and the shell is the default shell (= Erlang shell).
   211→                %% To be exact, eval the term as an Erlang term (but not using the
   212→                %% ?DEFAULT_SHELL directly). This disables banner, prompts and such.
   213→                %% The standard I/O is directed from/to the channel ChannelId.
   214→                exec_in_erlang_default_shell(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, WantReply, S1);
   215→
   216→            undefined ->
   217→                %% Exec called, but the a shell other than the default shell is defined.
   218→                %% No new exec shell is defined, so don't execute!
   219→                %% We don't know if it is intended to use the new shell or not.
   220→                {"Prohibited.", ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS, 1};
   221→
   222→            _ ->
   223→                %% Exec called and a Fun or MFA is defined to use.  The F communicates via
   224→                %% standard io:write/read.
   225→                %% Kept for compatibility.
   226→                S2 = start_exec_shell(ConnectionHandler, Cmd, S1),
   227→                ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
   228→                {ok, S2}
   229→        end
   230→    of
   231→        {Reply, Status, Type} ->
   232→            write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Type,
   233→                        unicode:characters_to_binary(Reply, utf8, out_enc(S1))),
   234→            ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
   235→            ssh_connection:exit_status(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Status),
   236→            ssh_connection:send_eof(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId),
   237→            {stop, ChannelId, S1#state{channel = ChannelId, cm = ConnectionHandler}};
   238→            
   239→        {ok, S} ->
   240→            {ok, S#state{channel = ChannelId,
   241→                         cm = ConnectionHandler}}
   242→    end;
   243→
   244→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _ConnectionHandler, {eof, _ChannelId}}, State) ->
   245→    {ok, State};
   246→
   247→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {signal, _, _}}, State) ->
   248→    %% Ignore signals according to RFC 4254 section 6.9.
   249→    {ok, State};
   250→
   251→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {exit_signal, ChannelId, _, Error, _}}, State) ->
   252→    Report = io_lib:format("Connection closed by peer ~n Error ~p~n",
   253→			   [Error]),
   254→    error_logger:error_report(Report),
   255→    {stop, ChannelId,  State};
   256→
   257→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {exit_status, ChannelId, 0}}, State) ->
   258→    {stop, ChannelId, State};
   259→
   260→handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {exit_status, ChannelId, Status}}, State) ->
   261→    
   262→    Report = io_lib:format("Connection closed by peer ~n Status ~p~n",
   263→			   [Status]),
   264→    error_logger:error_report(Report),
   265→    {stop, ChannelId, State}.

   268→%% Function: handle_msg(Args) -> {ok, State} | {stop, ChannelId, State}
   269→%%                        
   270→%% Description: Handles other channel messages.
   271→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   272→handle_msg({ssh_channel_up, ChannelId, ConnectionHandler},
   273→	   #state{channel = ChannelId,
   274→		  cm = ConnectionHandler} = State) ->
   275→    {ok,  State};
   276→
   277→handle_msg({Group, set_unicode_state, _Arg}, State) ->
   278→    Group ! {self(), set_unicode_state, false},
   279→    {ok, State};
   280→
   281→handle_msg({Group, get_unicode_state}, State) ->
   282→    Group ! {self(), get_unicode_state, false},
   283→    {ok, State};
   284→
   285→handle_msg({Group, get_terminal_state}, State) ->
   286→    Group ! {self(), get_terminal_state, #{ stdout => true, stdin => true }},
   287→    {ok, State};
   288→
   289→handle_msg({Group, tty_geometry}, #state{group = Group,
   290→					 pty = Pty
   291→					} = State) ->
   292→    case Pty of
   293→	#ssh_pty{width=Width,height=Height} ->
   294→	    Group ! {self(),tty_geometry,{Width,Height}};
   295→	_ ->
   296→	    %% This is a dirty fix of the problem with the otp ssh:shell
   297→	    %% client. That client will not allocate a tty, but someone
   298→	    %% asks for the tty_geometry just before every erlang prompt.
   299→	    %% If that question is not answered, there is a 2 sec timeout
   300→	    %% Until the prompt is seen by the user at the client side ...
   301→	    Group ! {self(),tty_geometry,{0,0}}
   302→    end,
   303→    {ok,State};
   304→    
   305→handle_msg({Group, Req}, #state{group = Group, buf = Buf, pty = Pty,
   306→                                cm = ConnectionHandler,
   307→                                channel = ChannelId} = State) ->
   308→    {Chars0, NewBuf} = io_request(Req, Buf, Pty, Group),
   309→    Chars = unicode:characters_to_binary(Chars0, utf8, out_enc(State)),
   310→    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Chars),
   311→    {ok, State#state{buf = NewBuf}};
   312→
   313→handle_msg({'EXIT', Group, Reason}, #state{group = Group,
   314→					    cm = ConnectionHandler,
   315→					    channel = ChannelId} = State) ->
   316→    ssh_connection:send_eof(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId),
   317→    ExitStatus = case Reason of
   318→                     normal ->
   319→                         0;
   320→                     {exit_status, V} when is_integer(V) ->
   321→                         V;
   322→                     _ ->
   323→                         ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS
   324→                 end,
   325→    ssh_connection:exit_status(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, ExitStatus),
   326→    {stop, ChannelId, State};
   327→
   328→handle_msg(_, State) ->
   329→    {ok, State}.

   338→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   339→%%% Internal functions
   340→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   341→
   342→claim_encoding(<<"/", _/binary>>) ->
   343→    %% If the locale value begins with a slash, it is interpreted
   344→    %% as the pathname of a file that was created in the output format
   345→    %% used by the localedef utility; see OUTPUT FILES under localedef.
   346→    %% Referencing such a pathname will result in that locale being used
   347→    %% for the indicated category.
   348→    undefined;
   349→
   350→claim_encoding(EnvValue) ->
   351→    %% If the locale value has the form:
   352→    %%      language[_territory][.codeset]
   353→    %% it refers to an implementation-provided locale, where settings of
   354→    %% language, territory and codeset are implementation-dependent. 
   355→    try string:tokens(binary_to_list(EnvValue), ".")
   356→    of
   357→        [_,"UTF-8"] -> {ok,utf8};
   358→        [_,"ISO-8859-1"] -> {ok,latin1};  % There are -1 ... -16  called latin1..latin16
   359→        _ -> undefined
   360→    catch
   361→        _:_ -> undefined
   362→    end.
   363→
   364→
   365→guess_encoding(Data0, #state{encoding = PeerEnc0,
   366→                             deduced_encoding = TestEnc0} = State) ->
   367→    Enc =
   368→        case {PeerEnc0,TestEnc0} of
   369→            {latin1,_} -> latin1;
   370→            {_,latin1} -> latin1;
   371→            _ -> case unicode:characters_to_binary(Data0, utf8, utf8) of
   372→                     Data0 -> utf8;
   373→                     _ -> latin1
   374→                 end
   375→        end,
   376→    case TestEnc0 of
   377→        Enc ->
   378→            {Enc, State};
   379→        latin1 ->
   380→            {Enc, State};
   381→        utf8 when Enc==latin1 ->
   382→            {Enc, State#state{deduced_encoding=latin1}};
   383→        undefined ->
   384→            {Enc, State#state{deduced_encoding=Enc}}
   385→    end.
   386→
   387→
   388→out_enc(#state{encoding = PeerEnc,
   389→               deduced_encoding = DeducedEnc}) ->
   390→    case DeducedEnc of
   391→        undefined -> PeerEnc;
   392→        _ -> DeducedEnc
   393→    end.

   395→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   396→
   397→to_group([], _Group, _Dumb) ->
   398→    ok;
   399→to_group([$\^C | Tail], Group, Dumb) ->
   400→    exit(Group, interrupt),
   401→    to_group(Tail, Group, Dumb);
   402→to_group(Data, Group, Dumb) ->
   403→    Func = fun(C) -> C /= $\^C end,
   404→    Tail = case lists:splitwith(Func, Data) of
   405→        {[], Right} ->
   406→            Right;
   407→        {Left, Right} ->
   408→            %% Filter out escape sequences, only support Ctrl sequences
   409→            Left1 = if Dumb -> replace_escapes(Left); true -> Left end,
   410→            Group ! {self(), {data, Left1}},
   411→            Right
   412→    end,
   413→    to_group(Tail, Group, Dumb).
   414→replace_escapes(Data) ->
   415→    lists:flatten([ if C =:= 27 ->
   416→        [$^,C+64];
   417→         true -> C
   418→    end || C <- Data]).

   420→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   421→%%% io_request, handle io requests from the user process,
   422→%%% Note, this is not the real I/O-protocol, but the mockup version
   423→%%% used between edlin and a user_driver. The protocol tags are
   424→%%% similar, but the message set is different. 
   425→%%% The protocol only exists internally between edlin and a character
   426→%%% displaying device...
   427→%%% We are *not* really unicode aware yet, we just filter away characters 
   428→%%% beyond the latin1 range. We however handle the unicode binaries...
   429→io_request({window_change, OldTty}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   430→    window_change(Tty, OldTty, Buf);
   431→io_request({put_chars, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   432→    put_chars(bin_to_list(Cs), Buf, Tty);
   433→io_request({put_chars, unicode, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   434→    put_chars(unicode:characters_to_list(Cs,unicode), Buf, Tty);
   435→io_request({put_expand, unicode, Expand, _N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   436→    insert_chars(unicode:characters_to_list("\n"++Expand, unicode), Buf, Tty);
   437→io_request({insert_chars, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   438→    insert_chars(bin_to_list(Cs), Buf, Tty);
   439→io_request({insert_chars, unicode, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   440→    insert_chars(unicode:characters_to_list(Cs,unicode), Buf, Tty);
   441→io_request({move_rel, N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   442→    move_rel(N, Buf, Tty);
   443→io_request({move_line, N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   444→    move_line(N, Buf, Tty);
   445→io_request({move_combo, L, V, R}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   446→    {ML, Buf1} = move_rel(L, Buf, Tty),
   447→    {MV, Buf2} = move_line(V, Buf1, Tty),
   448→    {MR, Buf3} = move_rel(R, Buf2, Tty),
   449→    {[ML,MV,MR], Buf3};
   450→io_request(new_prompt, _Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
   451→    {[], {[], {[],[]}, [], 0 }};
   452→io_request(delete_line, {_, {_, _}, _, Col}, Tty, _Group) ->
   453→    MoveToBeg = move_cursor(Col, 0, Tty),
   454→    {[MoveToBeg, "\e[J"],
   455→     {[],{[],[]},[],0}};
   456→io_request({redraw_prompt, Pbs, Pbs2, {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA}}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   457→    {ClearLine, Cleared} = io_request(delete_line, Buf, Tty, _Group),
   458→    CL = lists:reverse(Bef,Aft),
   459→    Text = Pbs ++ lists:flatten(lists:join("\n"++Pbs2, lists:reverse(LB)++[CL|LA])),
   460→    Moves = if LA /= [] ->
   461→                    [Last|_] = lists:reverse(LA),
   462→                    {move_combo, -length(Last), -length(LA), length(Bef)};
   463→               true ->
   464→                    {move_rel, -length(Aft)}
   465→            end,
   466→    {T, InsertedText} = io_request({insert_chars, unicode:characters_to_binary(Text)}, Cleared, Tty, _Group),
   467→    {M, Moved} = io_request(Moves, InsertedText, Tty, _Group),
   468→    {[ClearLine, T, M], Moved};
   469→io_request({delete_chars,N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
   470→    delete_chars(N, Buf, Tty);
   471→io_request(clear, Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
   472→    {"\e[H\e[2J", Buf};
   473→io_request(beep, Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
   474→    {[7], Buf};
   475→
   476→%% New in R12
   477→io_request({get_geometry,columns},Buf,Tty, _Group) ->
   478→    {ok, Tty#ssh_pty.width, Buf};
   479→io_request({get_geometry,rows},Buf,Tty, _Group) ->
   480→    {ok, Tty#ssh_pty.height, Buf};
   481→io_request({requests,Rs}, Buf, Tty, Group) ->
   482→    io_requests(Rs, Buf, Tty, [], Group);
   483→io_request(tty_geometry, Buf, Tty, Group) ->
   484→    io_requests([{move_rel, 0}, {put_chars, unicode, [10]}],
   485→                Buf, Tty, [], Group);
   486→
   487→%% New in 18
   488→io_request({put_chars_sync, Class, Cs, Reply}, Buf, Tty, Group) ->
   489→    %% We handle these asynchronous for now, if we need output guarantees
   490→    %% we have to handle these synchronously
   491→    Group ! {reply, Reply, ok},
   492→    io_request({put_chars, Class, Cs}, Buf, Tty, Group);
   493→
   494→io_request(_R, Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
   495→    {[], Buf}.
   496→
   497→io_requests([R|Rs], Buf, Tty, Acc, Group) ->
   498→    {Chars, NewBuf} = io_request(R, Buf, Tty, Group),
   499→    io_requests(Rs, NewBuf, Tty, [Acc|Chars], Group);
   500→io_requests([], Buf, _Tty, Acc, _Group) ->
   501→    {Acc, Buf}.

   503→%%% return commands for cursor navigation, assume everything is ansi
   504→%%% (vt100), add clauses for other terminal types if needed
   505→ansi_tty(N, L) ->
   506→    ["\e[", integer_to_list(N), L].
   507→
   508→get_tty_command(up, N, _TerminalType) ->
   509→    ansi_tty(N, $A);
   510→get_tty_command(down, N, _TerminalType) ->
   511→    ansi_tty(N, $B);
   512→get_tty_command(right, N, _TerminalType) ->
   513→    ansi_tty(N, $C);
   514→get_tty_command(left, N, _TerminalType) ->
   515→    ansi_tty(N, $D).

   517→
   518→-define(PAD, 10).
   519→-define(TABWIDTH, 8).
   520→
   521→%% convert input characters to buffer and to writeout
   522→%% Note that Bef is reversed but Aft is not
   523→%% (this is handy; the head is always next to the cursor)
   524→conv_buf([], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, _Tty) ->
   525→    {{LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, lists:reverse(AccWrite)};
   526→conv_buf([13, 10 | Rest], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, Tty = #ssh_pty{width = W}) ->
   527→    conv_buf(Rest, {[lists:reverse(Bef)|LB], {[], tl2(Aft)}, LA, Col+(W-(Col rem W))}, [10, 13 | AccWrite], Tty);
   528→conv_buf([13 | Rest], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, Tty = #ssh_pty{width = W}) ->
   529→    conv_buf(Rest, {[lists:reverse(Bef)|LB], {[], tl1(Aft)}, LA, Col+(W-(Col rem W))}, [13 | AccWrite], Tty);
   530→conv_buf([10 | Rest],{LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite0, Tty = #ssh_pty{width = W}) ->
   531→    AccWrite =
   532→        case pty_opt(onlcr,Tty) of
   533→            0 -> [10 | AccWrite0];
   534→            1 -> [10,13 | AccWrite0];
   535→            undefined -> [10 | AccWrite0]
   536→        end,
   537→    conv_buf(Rest, {[lists:reverse(Bef)|LB], {[], tl1(Aft)}, LA, Col+(W - (Col rem W))}, AccWrite, Tty);
   538→conv_buf([C | Rest], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, Tty) ->
   539→    conv_buf(Rest, {LB, {[C|Bef], tl1(Aft)}, LA, Col+1}, [C | AccWrite], Tty).
   540→
   541→%%% put characters before the prompt
   542→put_chars(Chars, Buf, Tty) ->
   543→    Dumb = get_dumb(Tty),
   544→    case Buf of
   545→        {[],{[],[]},[],_} -> {_, WriteBuf} = conv_buf(Chars, Buf, [], Tty),
   546→            {WriteBuf, Buf};
   547→        _ when Dumb =:= false ->
   548→            {Delete, DeletedState} = io_request(delete_line, Buf, Tty, []),
   549→            {_, PutBuffer} = conv_buf(Chars, DeletedState, [], Tty),
   550→            {Redraw, _} = io_request(redraw_prompt_pre_deleted, Buf, Tty, []),
   551→            {[Delete, PutBuffer, Redraw], Buf};
   552→        _ ->
   553→            %% When we have a dumb terminal, we get messages via put_chars requests
   554→            %% so state should be empty {[],{[],[]},[],_},
   555→            %% but if we end up here its not, so keep the state
   556→            {_, WriteBuf} = conv_buf(Chars, Buf, [], Tty),
   557→            {WriteBuf, Buf}
   558→    end.
   559→
   560→%%% insert character at current position
   561→insert_chars([], Buf, _Tty) ->
   562→    {[], Buf};
   563→insert_chars(Chars, {_LB,{_Bef, Aft},LA, _Col}=Buf, Tty) ->
   564→    {{NewLB, {NewBef, _NewAft}, _NewLA, NewCol}, WriteBuf} = conv_buf(Chars, Buf, [], Tty),
   565→    M = move_cursor(special_at_width(NewCol+length(Aft), Tty), NewCol, Tty),
   566→    {[WriteBuf, Aft | M], {NewLB,{NewBef, Aft},LA, NewCol}}.
   567→
   568→%%% delete characters at current position, (backwards if negative argument)
   569→delete_chars(0, {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}, _Tty) ->
   570→    {[], {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}};
   571→delete_chars(N, {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}, Tty) when N > 0 ->
   572→    NewAft = nthtail(N, Aft),
   573→    M = move_cursor(Col + length(NewAft) + N, Col, Tty),
   574→    {[NewAft, lists:duplicate(N, $ ) | M],
   575→     {LB,{Bef, NewAft},LA, Col}};
   576→delete_chars(N, {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}, Tty) -> % N < 0
   577→    NewBef = nthtail(-N, Bef),
   578→    NewCol = case Col + N of V when V >= 0 -> V; _ -> 0 end,
   579→    M1 = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
   580→    M2 = move_cursor(special_at_width(NewCol+length(Aft)-N, Tty), NewCol, Tty),
   581→    {[M1, Aft, lists:duplicate(-N, $ ) | M2],
   582→     {LB,{NewBef, Aft},LA, NewCol}}.
   583→
   584→%%% Window change, redraw the current line (and clear out after it
   585→%%% if current window is wider than previous)
   586→window_change(Tty, OldTty, Buf)
   587→  when OldTty#ssh_pty.width == Tty#ssh_pty.width ->
   588→     %% No line width change
   589→    {[], Buf};
   590→window_change(Tty, OldTty, {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}) ->
   591→    case OldTty#ssh_pty.width - Tty#ssh_pty.width of
   592→        0 ->
   593→            %% No line width change
   594→            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}};
   595→
   596→        DeltaW0 when DeltaW0 < 0,
   597→                     Aft == [] ->
   598→            % Line width is decreased, cursor is at end of input
   599→            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}};
   600→
   601→        DeltaW0 when DeltaW0 < 0,
   602→                     Aft =/= [] ->
   603→            % Line width is decreased, cursor is not at end of input
   604→            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}};
   605→
   606→        DeltaW0 when DeltaW0 > 0 ->
   607→            % Line width is increased
   608→            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}}
   609→        end.
   610→
   611→%% move around in buffer, respecting pad characters
   612→step_over(0, {LB, {Bef, [?PAD |Aft]}, LA, Col}) ->
   613→    {LB, {[?PAD | Bef], Aft}, LA, Col+1};
   614→step_over(0, {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}) ->
   615→    {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col};
   616→step_over(N, {LB, {[C | Bef], Aft}, LA, Col}) when N < 0 ->
   617→    N1 = ifelse(C == ?PAD, N, N+1),
   618→    step_over(N1, {LB, {Bef, [C | Aft]}, LA, Col-1});
   619→step_over(N, {LB, {Bef, [C | Aft]}, LA, Col}) when N > 0 ->
   620→    N1 = ifelse(C == ?PAD, N, N-1),
   621→    step_over(N1, {LB, {[C | Bef], Aft}, LA, Col+1}).
   622→
   623→%%% an empty line buffer
   624→empty_buf() -> {[], {[], []}, [], 0}.
   625→
   626→%%% col and row from position with given width
   627→col(N, W) -> N rem W.
   628→row(N, W) -> N div W.
   629→
   630→%%% move relative N characters
   631→move_rel(N, {_LB, {_Bef, _Aft}, _LA, Col}=Buf, Tty) ->
   632→    {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol} = step_over(N, Buf),
   633→    M = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
   634→    {M, {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol}}.
   635→
   636→move_line(V, {_LB, {_Bef, _Aft}, _LA, Col}, Tty = #ssh_pty{width=W})
   637→        when V < 0, length(_LB) >= -V ->
   638→    {LinesJumped, [B|NewLB]} = lists:split(-V -1, _LB),
   639→    CL = lists:reverse(_Bef,_Aft),
   640→    NewLA = lists:reverse([CL|LinesJumped], _LA),
   641→    {NewBB, NewAft} = lists:split(min(length(_Bef),length(B)), B),
   642→    NewBef = lists:reverse(NewBB),
   643→    NewCol = Col - length(_Bef) - lists:sum([((length(L)-1) div W)*W + W || L <- [B|LinesJumped]]) + length(NewBB),
   644→    M = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
   645→    {M, {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol}};
   646→move_line(V, {_LB, {_Bef, _Aft}, _LA, Col}, Tty = #ssh_pty{width=W})
   647→        when V > 0, length(_LA) >= V ->
   648→    {LinesJumped, [A|NewLA]} = lists:split(V -1, _LA),
   649→    CL = lists:reverse(_Bef,_Aft),
   650→    NewLB = lists:reverse([CL|LinesJumped],_LB),
   651→    {NewBB, NewAft} = lists:split(min(length(_Bef),length(A)), A),
   652→    NewBef = lists:reverse(NewBB),
   653→    NewCol = Col - length(_Bef) + lists:sum([((length(L)-1) div W)*W + W || L <- [CL|LinesJumped]]) + length(NewBB),
   654→    M = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
   655→    {M, {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol}};
   656→move_line(_, Buf, _) ->
   657→    {"", Buf}.
   658→%%% give move command for tty
   659→move_cursor(A, A, _Tty) ->
   660→    [];
   661→move_cursor(From, To, #ssh_pty{width=Width, term=Type}) ->
   662→    Tcol = case col(To, Width) - col(From, Width) of
   663→	       0 -> "";
   664→	       I when I < 0 -> get_tty_command(left, -I, Type);
   665→	       I -> get_tty_command(right, I, Type)
   666→	end,
   667→    Trow = case row(To, Width) - row(From, Width) of
   668→	       0 -> "";
   669→	       J when J < 0 -> get_tty_command(up, -J, Type);
   670→	       J -> get_tty_command(down, J, Type)
   671→	   end,
   672→    [Tcol | Trow].
   673→
   674→%%% Caution for line "breaks"
   675→special_at_width(From0, #ssh_pty{width=Width}) when (From0 rem Width) == 0 -> From0 - 1;
   676→special_at_width(From0, _) -> From0.
   677→
   678→%% %%% write out characters
   679→%% %%% make sure that there is data to send
   680→%% %%% before calling ssh_connection:send
   681→write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Chars) ->
   682→    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, ?SSH_EXTENDED_DATA_DEFAULT, Chars).
   683→
   684→write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Type, Chars) ->
   685→    case has_chars(Chars) of
   686→        false -> ok;
   687→        true -> ssh_connection:send(ConnectionHandler,
   688→                                    ChannelId,
   689→                                    Type,
   690→                                    Chars)
   691→    end.
   692→
   693→has_chars([C|_]) when is_integer(C) -> true;
   694→has_chars([H|T]) when is_list(H) ; is_binary(H) -> has_chars(H) orelse has_chars(T);
   695→has_chars(<<_:8,_/binary>>) -> true;
   696→has_chars(_) -> false.
   697→    
   698→
   699→%%% tail, works with empty lists
   700→tl1([_|A]) -> A;
   701→tl1(_) -> [].
   702→
   703→%%% second tail
   704→tl2([_,_|A]) -> A;
   705→tl2(_) -> [].
   706→
   707→%%% nthtail as in lists, but no badarg if n > the length of list
   708→nthtail(0, A) -> A;
   709→nthtail(N, [_ | A]) when N > 0 -> nthtail(N-1, A);
   710→nthtail(_, _) -> [].
   711→
   712→ifelse(Cond, A, B) ->
   713→    case Cond of
   714→	true -> A;
   715→	_ -> B
   716→    end.	    
   717→
   718→bin_to_list(B) when is_binary(B) ->
   719→    binary_to_list(B);
   720→bin_to_list(L) when is_list(L) ->
   721→    lists:flatten([bin_to_list(A) || A <- L]);
   722→bin_to_list(I) when is_integer(I) ->
   723→    I.
   724→
   725→
   726→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   727→start_shell(ConnectionHandler, State) ->
   728→    ShellSpawner =
   729→        case State#state.shell of
   730→            Shell when is_function(Shell, 1) ->
   731→                [{user,User}] = ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [user]),
   732→                fun() -> Shell(User) end;
   733→            Shell when is_function(Shell, 2) ->
   734→                ConnectionInfo =
   735→                    ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [peer, user]),
   736→                User = proplists:get_value(user, ConnectionInfo),
   737→                {_, PeerAddr} = proplists:get_value(peer, ConnectionInfo),
   738→                fun() -> Shell(User, PeerAddr) end;
   739→            {_,_,_} = Shell ->
   740→                Shell
   741→        end,
   742→    State#state{group = group:start(self(), ShellSpawner,
   743→                                    [{dumb, get_dumb(State#state.pty)},{expand_below, false},
   744→                                     {echo, get_echo(State#state.pty)}]),
   745→                buf = empty_buf()}.
   746→
   747→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   748→start_exec_shell(ConnectionHandler, Cmd, State) ->
   749→    ExecShellSpawner =
   750→        case State#state.exec of
   751→            ExecShell when is_function(ExecShell, 1) ->
   752→                fun() -> ExecShell(Cmd) end;
   753→            ExecShell when is_function(ExecShell, 2) ->
   754→                [{user,User}] = ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [user]),
   755→                fun() -> ExecShell(Cmd, User) end;
   756→            ExecShell when is_function(ExecShell, 3) ->
   757→                ConnectionInfo =
   758→                    ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [peer, user]),
   759→                User = proplists:get_value(user, ConnectionInfo),
   760→                {_, PeerAddr} = proplists:get_value(peer, ConnectionInfo),
   761→                fun() -> ExecShell(Cmd, User, PeerAddr) end;
   762→            {M,F,A} ->
   763→                {M, F, A++[Cmd]}
   764→        end,
   765→    State#state{group = group:start(self(), ExecShellSpawner, [{expand_below, false},
   766→                                                               {echo,false}]),
   767→                buf = empty_buf()}.
   768→
   769→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   770→exec_in_erlang_default_shell(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, WantReply, State) ->
   771→    exec_in_self_group(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, WantReply, State,
   772→      fun() ->
   773→              eval(parse(scan(Cmd)))
   774→      end).
   775→
   776→
   777→scan(Cmd) ->
   778→    erl_scan:string(Cmd). 
   779→
   780→parse({ok, Tokens, _}) ->
   781→    erl_parse:parse_exprs(Tokens);
   782→parse({error, {_,erl_scan,Cause}, _}) ->
   783→    {error, erl_scan:format_error(Cause)}.
   784→
   785→eval({ok, Expr_list}) ->
   786→    {value, Value, _NewBindings} = erl_eval:exprs(Expr_list, erl_eval:new_bindings()),
   787→    {ok, Value};
   788→eval({error, {_,erl_parse,Cause}}) ->
   789→    {error, erl_parse:format_error(Cause)};
   790→eval({error,Error}) ->
   791→    {error, Error}.
   792→
   793→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   794→exec_direct(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, ExecSpec, WantReply, State) ->
   795→    Fun =
   796→        fun() ->
   797→                if
   798→                    is_function(ExecSpec, 1) ->
   799→                        ExecSpec(Cmd);
   800→
   801→                    is_function(ExecSpec, 2) ->
   802→                        [{user,User}] = ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [user]),
   803→                        ExecSpec(Cmd, User);
   804→
   805→                    is_function(ExecSpec, 3) ->
   806→                        ConnectionInfo =
   807→                            ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [peer, user]),
   808→                        User = proplists:get_value(user, ConnectionInfo),
   809→                        {_, PeerAddr} = proplists:get_value(peer, ConnectionInfo),
   810→                        ExecSpec(Cmd, User, PeerAddr);
   811→
   812→                    true ->
   813→                        {error, "Bad exec fun in server"}
   814→                end
   815→        end,
   816→    exec_in_self_group(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, WantReply, State, Fun).
   817→
   818→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   819→%% Help for directing stdin and stdout from and to the channel from/to the client
   820→%%
   821→exec_in_self_group(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, WantReply, State, Fun) ->
   822→    Exec =
   823→        fun() ->
   824→                spawn(
   825→                  fun() ->
   826→                          case try
   827→                                   ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
   828→                                   Fun()
   829→                               of
   830→                                   {ok, Result} ->
   831→                                       {ok, Result};
   832→                                   {error, Error} ->
   833→                                       {error, Error};
   834→                                   X ->
   835→                                       {error, "Bad exec fun in server. Invalid return value: "++t2str(X)}
   836→                               catch error:Err ->
   837→                                       {error,Err};
   838→                                     Cls:Exp ->
   839→                                       {error,{Cls,Exp}}
   840→                               end
   841→                          of
   842→                              {ok,Str} ->
   843→                                  write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, t2str(Str));
   844→                              {error, Str} ->
   845→                                  write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, 1, "**Error** "++t2str(Str)),
   846→                                  exit({exit_status, ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS})
   847→                          end
   848→                  end)
   849→        end,
   850→    {ok, State#state{group = group:start(self(), Exec, [{expand_below, false},
   851→                                                        {echo,false}]),
   852→                     buf = empty_buf()}}.
   853→    
   854→
   855→t2str(T) -> try io_lib:format("~s",[T])
   856→            catch _:_ -> io_lib:format("~p",[T])
   857→            end.
   858→
   859→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   860→get_dumb(Tty) ->
   861→    try
   862→        Tty#ssh_pty.term =:= "dumb"
   863→    catch
   864→        _:_ -> false
   865→    end.
   866→
   867→% Pty can be undefined if the client never sets any pty options before
   868→% starting the shell.
   869→get_echo(Tty) ->
   870→    case pty_opt(echo,Tty) of
   871→        0 -> false;
   872→        1 -> true;
   873→        undefined -> true
   874→    end.
   875→
   876→% Group is undefined if the pty options are sent between open and
   877→% shell messages.
   878→set_echo(#state{group = undefined}) ->
   879→    ok;
   880→set_echo(#state{group = Group, pty = Pty}) ->
   881→    Echo = get_echo(Pty),
   882→    Group ! {self(), echo, Echo}.
   883→
   884→not_zero(0, B) -> 
   885→    B;
   886→not_zero(A, _) -> 
   887→    A.
   888→
   889→%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
   890→pty_opt(Name, Tty) ->
   891→    try
   892→        proplists:get_value(Name, Tty#ssh_pty.modes, undefined)
   893→    catch
   894→        _:_ -> undefined
   895→    end.
   896→
   897→%%%################################################################
   898→%%%#
   899→%%%# Tracing
   900→%%%#
   901→
   902→ssh_dbg_trace_points() -> [terminate, cli, cli_details].
   903→
   904→ssh_dbg_flags(cli) -> [c];
   905→ssh_dbg_flags(terminate) -> [c].
   906→
   907→ssh_dbg_on(cli) -> dbg:tp(?MODULE,handle_ssh_msg,2,x),
   908→                   dbg:tp(?MODULE,write_chars,4,x);
   909→ssh_dbg_on(cli_details) -> dbg:tp(?MODULE,handle_msg,2,x);
   910→ssh_dbg_on(terminate) -> dbg:tp(?MODULE,  terminate, 2, x).
   911→
   912→
   913→ssh_dbg_off(cli) -> dbg:ctpg(?MODULE,handle_ssh_msg,2),
   914→                    dbg:ctpg(?MODULE,write_chars,4);
   915→ssh_dbg_off(cli_details) -> dbg:ctpg(?MODULE,handle_msg,2);
   916→ssh_dbg_off(terminate) -> dbg:ctpg(?MODULE, terminate, 2).
   917→
   918→
   919→ssh_dbg_format(cli, {call,{?MODULE,handle_ssh_msg,
   920→                           [{ssh_cm, _ConnectionHandler, Request},
   921→                            S = #state{channel=Ch}]}}) when is_tuple(Request) ->
   922→    [io_lib:format("CLI conn ~p chan ~p, req ~p", 
   923→                   [self(),Ch,element(1,Request)]),
   924→     case Request of
   925→         {window_change, ChannelId, Width, Height, PixWidth, PixHeight} ->
   926→             fmt_kv([{channel_id,ChannelId}, 
   927→                     {width,Width}, {height,Height},
   928→                     {pix_width,PixWidth}, {pixel_hight,PixHeight}]);
   929→
   930→         {env, ChannelId, WantReply, Var, Value} ->
   931→             fmt_kv([{channel_id,ChannelId}, {want_reply,WantReply}, {Var,Value}]);
   932→
   933→         {exec, ChannelId, WantReply, Cmd} ->
   934→             fmt_kv([{channel_id,ChannelId}, {want_reply,WantReply}, {command,Cmd}]);
   935→
   936→         {pty, ChannelId, WantReply,
   937→          {TermName, Width, Height, PixWidth, PixHeight, Modes}} ->
   938→             fmt_kv([{channel_id,ChannelId}, {want_reply,WantReply}, 
   939→                     {term,TermName},
   940→                     {width,Width}, {height,Height}, {pix_width,PixWidth}, {pixel_hight,PixHeight},
   941→                     {pty_opts, Modes}]);
   942→
   943→         {data, ChannelId, Type, Data} -> 
   944→             fmt_kv([{channel_id,ChannelId},
   945→                     {type, type(Type)},
   946→                     {data, us, ssh_dbg:shrink_bin(Data)},
   947→                     {hex, h, Data}
   948→                    ]);
   949→
   950→         {shell, ChannelId, WantReply} ->
   951→             fmt_kv([{channel_id,ChannelId},
   952→                     {want_reply,WantReply},
   953→                     {encoding, S#state.encoding},
   954→                     {pty, S#state.pty}
   955→                    ]);
   956→
   957→         _ ->
   958→             io_lib:format("~nunder construction:~nRequest = ~p",[Request])
   959→     end];
   960→ssh_dbg_format(cli, {call,{?MODULE,handle_ssh_msg,_}}) -> skip;
   961→ssh_dbg_format(cli, {return_from,{?MODULE,handle_ssh_msg,2},_Result}) -> skip;
   962→
   963→ssh_dbg_format(cli, {call,{?MODULE,write_chars, [C, Ch, Type, Chars]}}) ->
   964→    [io_lib:format("CLI conn ~p chan ~p reply", [C,Ch]),
   965→     fmt_kv([{channel_id,Ch},
   966→             {type, type(Type)},
   967→             {data, us, ssh_dbg:shrink_bin(Chars)},
   968→             {hex, h, Chars}
   969→            ])];
   970→ssh_dbg_format(cli, {return_from,{?MODULE,write_chars,4},_Result}) -> skip;
   971→
   972→
   973→ssh_dbg_format(cli_details, {call,{?MODULE,handle_msg,
   974→                                   [{Group,Arg}, #state{channel=Ch}]}}) ->
   975→    [io_lib:format("CLI detail conn ~p chan ~p group ~p",
   976→                   ['?', Ch, Group]),
   977→     case Arg of
   978→         {put_chars_sync,Class,Cs,Reply} ->
   979→             fmt_kv([{op, put_chars_sync},
   980→                     {class, Class},
   981→                     {data, us, ssh_dbg:shrink_bin(Cs)},
   982→                     {hex, h, Cs},
   983→                     {reply, Reply}]);
   984→         _ ->
   985→             io_lib:format("~nunder construction:~nRequest = ~p",[Arg])
   986→     end];
   987→ssh_dbg_format(cli_details, {call,{?MODULE,handle_msg,_}}) -> skip;
   988→ssh_dbg_format(cli_details, {return_from,{?MODULE,handle_msg,2},_Result}) -> skip;
   989→
   990→ssh_dbg_format(terminate, {call, {?MODULE,terminate, [Reason, State]}}) ->
   991→    ["Cli Terminating:\n",
   992→     io_lib:format("Reason: ~p,~nState:~n~s", [Reason, wr_record(State)])
   993→    ];
   994→ssh_dbg_format(terminate, {return_from, {?MODULE,terminate,2}, _Ret}) ->
   995→    skip.
   996→
   997→
   998→?wr_record(state).
   999→
  1000→fmt_kv(KVs) -> lists:map(fun fmt_kv1/1, KVs).
  1001→
  1002→fmt_kv1({K,V})   -> io_lib:format("~n~p: ~p",[K,V]);
  1003→fmt_kv1({K,s,V}) -> io_lib:format("~n~p: ~s",[K,V]);
  1004→fmt_kv1({K,us,V}) -> io_lib:format("~n~p: ~ts",[K,V]);
  1005→fmt_kv1({K,h,V}) -> io_lib:format("~n~p: ~s",[K, [$\n|ssh_dbg:hex_dump(V)]]).
  1006→
  1007→type(0) -> "0 (normal data)";
  1008→type(1) -> "1 (extended data, i.e. errors)";
  1009→type(T) -> T.
  1010→

%%

%%
%% Description: a gen_server implementing a simple
%% terminal (using the group module) for a CLI
%% over SSH

-module(ssh_cli).
-moduledoc false.

-behaviour(ssh_server_channel).

-include("ssh.hrl").
-include("ssh_connect.hrl").

%% ssh_server_channel callbacks
-export([init/1, handle_ssh_msg/2, handle_msg/2, terminate/2]).

-behaviour(ssh_dbg).
-export([ssh_dbg_trace_points/0, ssh_dbg_flags/1, ssh_dbg_on/1, ssh_dbg_off/1, ssh_dbg_format/2]).

%% state
-record(state, {
	  cm,
	  channel,
	  pty,
          encoding,
          deduced_encoding, % OpenSSH sometimes lies about its encodeing. This variable
                            % is for the process of guessing the peer encoding, taylord
                            % after the behaviour of openssh.  If it says latin1 it is so.
                            % It there arrives characters encoded in latin1 it is so. Otherwise
                            % assume utf8 until otherwise is proved.
	  group,
	  buf,
	  shell,
	  exec
	 }).

-define(EXEC_ERROR_STATUS, 255).

%%====================================================================
%% ssh_server_channel callbacks
%%====================================================================

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Function: init(Args) -> {ok, State} 
%%                        
%% Description: Initiates the CLI
%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
init([Shell, Exec]) ->
    {ok, #state{shell = Shell, exec = Exec}};
init([Shell]) ->
    {ok, #state{shell = Shell}}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Function: handle_ssh_msg(Args) -> {ok, State} | {stop, ChannelId, State}
%%                        
%% Description: Handles channel messages received on the ssh-connection.
%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _ConnectionHandler,
		{data, _ChannelId, _Type, Data}}, 
	       #state{group = Group} = State0) ->
    {Enc, State} = guess_encoding(Data, State0),
    List = unicode:characters_to_list(Data, Enc),
    to_group(List, Group, get_dumb(State#state.pty)),
    {ok, State};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,
		{pty, ChannelId, WantReply, 
		 {TermName, Width, Height, PixWidth, PixHeight, Modes}}}, 
	       State0) ->
    State = State0#state{pty = 
			 #ssh_pty{term = TermName,
				  width =  not_zero(Width, 80),
				  height = not_zero(Height, 24),
				  pixel_width = PixWidth,
				  pixel_height = PixHeight,
                  modes = Modes},
             buf = empty_buf()},
    set_echo(State),
    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply,
				 success, ChannelId),
    {ok, State};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,
	    {env, ChannelId, WantReply, Var, Value}}, State = #state{encoding=Enc0}) ->
    %% It is not as simple as it sounds to set environment variables
    %% in the server.
    %% The (OS) env vars should be per per Channel; otherwise anyone
    %% could affect anyone other's variables.
    %% Therefore this clause always return a failure.
    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler,
				 WantReply, failure, ChannelId),

    %% https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/7908799/xbd/envvar.html
    %% LANG
    %%     This variable determines the locale category for native language,
    %%     local customs and coded character set in the absence of the LC_ALL
    %%     and other LC_* (LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY,
    %%     LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) environment variables. This can be used by
    %%     applications to determine the language to use for error messages
    %%     and instructions, collating sequences, date formats, and so forth. 
    %% LC_ALL
    %%     This variable determines the values for all locale categories. The
    %%     value of the LC_ALL environment variable has precedence over any of
    %%     the other environment variables starting with LC_ (LC_COLLATE,
    %%     LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) and the
    %%     LANG environment variable.
    %% ...
    %%
    %%  The values of locale categories are determined by a precedence order;
    %%  the first condition met below determines the value:
    %%
    %%   1. If the LC_ALL environment variable is defined and is not null,
    %%      the value of LC_ALL is used.
    %%
    %%   2. If the LC_* environment variable ( LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES,
    %%      LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) is defined and is not null, the
    %%      value of the environment variable is used to initialise the category
    %%      that corresponds to the environment variable.
    %%
    %%   3. If the LANG environment variable is defined and is not null, the value
    %%      of the LANG environment variable is used.
    %%
    %%   4. If the LANG environment variable is not set or is set to the empty string,
    %%      the implementation-dependent default locale is used. 

    Enc =
        %% Rule 1 and 3 above says that LC_ALL has precedence over LANG. Since they
        %% arrives in different messages and in an undefined order, it is resolved
        %% like this:
        case Var of
            <<"LANG">> when Enc0==undefined ->
                %% No previous LC_ALL
                case claim_encoding(Value) of
                    {ok,Enc1} -> Enc1;
                    _ -> Enc0
                end;
            <<"LC_ALL">> ->
                %% Maybe or maybe not a LANG has been handled, LC_ALL doesn't care
                case claim_encoding(Value) of
                    {ok,Enc1} -> Enc1;
                    _ -> Enc0
                end;
            _ ->
                Enc0
        end,
    {ok, State#state{encoding=Enc}};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,
	    {window_change, ChannelId, Width, Height, PixWidth, PixHeight}},
	   #state{buf = Buf, pty = Pty0} = State) ->
    Pty = Pty0#ssh_pty{width = Width, height = Height,
		       pixel_width = PixWidth,
		       pixel_height = PixHeight},
    {Chars, NewBuf} = io_request({window_change, Pty0}, Buf, Pty, undefined),
    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Chars),
    {ok, State#state{pty = Pty, buf = NewBuf}};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,  {shell, ChannelId, WantReply}}, #state{shell=disabled} = State) ->
    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, 1, "Prohibited."),
    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
    ssh_connection:exit_status(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS),
    ssh_connection:send_eof(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId),
    {stop, ChannelId, State#state{channel = ChannelId, cm = ConnectionHandler}};
handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,  {shell, ChannelId, WantReply}}, State0) ->
    State = case State0#state.encoding of
                undefined -> State0#state{encoding = utf8};
                _-> State0
            end,
    NewState = start_shell(ConnectionHandler, State),
    ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
    {ok, NewState#state{channel = ChannelId,
			cm = ConnectionHandler}};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, ConnectionHandler,  {exec, ChannelId, WantReply, Cmd0}}, S0) ->
    {Enc,S1} = guess_encoding(Cmd0, S0),
    Cmd = unicode:characters_to_list(Cmd0, Enc),
    case
        case S1#state.exec of
            disabled ->
                {"Prohibited.", ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS, 1};

            {direct,F} ->
                %% Exec called and a Fun or MFA is defined to use.  The F returns the
                %% value to return.
                %% The standard I/O is directed from/to the channel ChannelId.
                exec_direct(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, F, WantReply, S1);

            undefined when S0#state.shell == ?DEFAULT_SHELL ; 
                           S0#state.shell == disabled ->
                %% Exec called and the shell is the default shell (= Erlang shell).
                %% To be exact, eval the term as an Erlang term (but not using the
                %% ?DEFAULT_SHELL directly). This disables banner, prompts and such.
                %% The standard I/O is directed from/to the channel ChannelId.
                exec_in_erlang_default_shell(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, WantReply, S1);

            undefined ->
                %% Exec called, but the a shell other than the default shell is defined.
                %% No new exec shell is defined, so don't execute!
                %% We don't know if it is intended to use the new shell or not.
                {"Prohibited.", ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS, 1};

            _ ->
                %% Exec called and a Fun or MFA is defined to use.  The F communicates via
                %% standard io:write/read.
                %% Kept for compatibility.
                S2 = start_exec_shell(ConnectionHandler, Cmd, S1),
                ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
                {ok, S2}
        end
    of
        {Reply, Status, Type} ->
            write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Type,
                        unicode:characters_to_binary(Reply, utf8, out_enc(S1))),
            ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
            ssh_connection:exit_status(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Status),
            ssh_connection:send_eof(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId),
            {stop, ChannelId, S1#state{channel = ChannelId, cm = ConnectionHandler}};
            
        {ok, S} ->
            {ok, S#state{channel = ChannelId,
                         cm = ConnectionHandler}}
    end;

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _ConnectionHandler, {eof, _ChannelId}}, State) ->
    {ok, State};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {signal, _, _}}, State) ->
    %% Ignore signals according to RFC 4254 section 6.9.
    {ok, State};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {exit_signal, ChannelId, _, Error, _}}, State) ->
    Report = io_lib:format("Connection closed by peer ~n Error ~p~n",
			   [Error]),
    error_logger:error_report(Report),
    {stop, ChannelId,  State};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {exit_status, ChannelId, 0}}, State) ->
    {stop, ChannelId, State};

handle_ssh_msg({ssh_cm, _, {exit_status, ChannelId, Status}}, State) ->
    
    Report = io_lib:format("Connection closed by peer ~n Status ~p~n",
			   [Status]),
    error_logger:error_report(Report),
    {stop, ChannelId, State}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Function: handle_msg(Args) -> {ok, State} | {stop, ChannelId, State}
%%                        
%% Description: Handles other channel messages.
%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
handle_msg({ssh_channel_up, ChannelId, ConnectionHandler},
	   #state{channel = ChannelId,
		  cm = ConnectionHandler} = State) ->
    {ok,  State};

handle_msg({Group, set_unicode_state, _Arg}, State) ->
    Group ! {self(), set_unicode_state, false},
    {ok, State};

handle_msg({Group, get_unicode_state}, State) ->
    Group ! {self(), get_unicode_state, false},
    {ok, State};

handle_msg({Group, get_terminal_state}, State) ->
    Group ! {self(), get_terminal_state, #{ stdout => true, stdin => true }},
    {ok, State};

handle_msg({Group, tty_geometry}, #state{group = Group,
					 pty = Pty
					} = State) ->
    case Pty of
	#ssh_pty{width=Width,height=Height} ->
	    Group ! {self(),tty_geometry,{Width,Height}};
	_ ->
	    %% This is a dirty fix of the problem with the otp ssh:shell
	    %% client. That client will not allocate a tty, but someone
	    %% asks for the tty_geometry just before every erlang prompt.
	    %% If that question is not answered, there is a 2 sec timeout
	    %% Until the prompt is seen by the user at the client side ...
	    Group ! {self(),tty_geometry,{0,0}}
    end,
    {ok,State};
    
handle_msg({Group, Req}, #state{group = Group, buf = Buf, pty = Pty,
                                cm = ConnectionHandler,
                                channel = ChannelId} = State) ->
    {Chars0, NewBuf} = io_request(Req, Buf, Pty, Group),
    Chars = unicode:characters_to_binary(Chars0, utf8, out_enc(State)),
    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Chars),
    {ok, State#state{buf = NewBuf}};

handle_msg({'EXIT', Group, Reason}, #state{group = Group,
					    cm = ConnectionHandler,
					    channel = ChannelId} = State) ->
    ssh_connection:send_eof(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId),
    ExitStatus = case Reason of
                     normal ->
                         0;
                     {exit_status, V} when is_integer(V) ->
                         V;
                     _ ->
                         ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS
                 end,
    ssh_connection:exit_status(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, ExitStatus),
    {stop, ChannelId, State};

handle_msg(_, State) ->
    {ok, State}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Function: terminate(Reason, State) -> void()
%% Description: Called when the channel process is trminated
%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
terminate(_Reason, _State) ->
    ok.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%%% Internal functions
%%--------------------------------------------------------------------

claim_encoding(<<"/", _/binary>>) ->
    %% If the locale value begins with a slash, it is interpreted
    %% as the pathname of a file that was created in the output format
    %% used by the localedef utility; see OUTPUT FILES under localedef.
    %% Referencing such a pathname will result in that locale being used
    %% for the indicated category.
    undefined;

claim_encoding(EnvValue) ->
    %% If the locale value has the form:
    %%      language[_territory][.codeset]
    %% it refers to an implementation-provided locale, where settings of
    %% language, territory and codeset are implementation-dependent. 
    try string:tokens(binary_to_list(EnvValue), ".")
    of
        [_,"UTF-8"] -> {ok,utf8};
        [_,"ISO-8859-1"] -> {ok,latin1};  % There are -1 ... -16  called latin1..latin16
        _ -> undefined
    catch
        _:_ -> undefined
    end.


guess_encoding(Data0, #state{encoding = PeerEnc0,
                             deduced_encoding = TestEnc0} = State) ->
    Enc =
        case {PeerEnc0,TestEnc0} of
            {latin1,_} -> latin1;
            {_,latin1} -> latin1;
            _ -> case unicode:characters_to_binary(Data0, utf8, utf8) of
                     Data0 -> utf8;
                     _ -> latin1
                 end
        end,
    case TestEnc0 of
        Enc ->
            {Enc, State};
        latin1 ->
            {Enc, State};
        utf8 when Enc==latin1 ->
            {Enc, State#state{deduced_encoding=latin1}};
        undefined ->
            {Enc, State#state{deduced_encoding=Enc}}
    end.


out_enc(#state{encoding = PeerEnc,
               deduced_encoding = DeducedEnc}) ->
    case DeducedEnc of
        undefined -> PeerEnc;
        _ -> DeducedEnc
    end.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------

to_group([], _Group, _Dumb) ->
    ok;
to_group([$\^C | Tail], Group, Dumb) ->
    exit(Group, interrupt),
    to_group(Tail, Group, Dumb);
to_group(Data, Group, Dumb) ->
    Func = fun(C) -> C /= $\^C end,
    Tail = case lists:splitwith(Func, Data) of
        {[], Right} ->
            Right;
        {Left, Right} ->
            %% Filter out escape sequences, only support Ctrl sequences
            Left1 = if Dumb -> replace_escapes(Left); true -> Left end,
            Group ! {self(), {data, Left1}},
            Right
    end,
    to_group(Tail, Group, Dumb).
replace_escapes(Data) ->
    lists:flatten([ if C =:= 27 ->
        [$^,C+64];
         true -> C
    end || C <- Data]).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%%% io_request, handle io requests from the user process,
%%% Note, this is not the real I/O-protocol, but the mockup version
%%% used between edlin and a user_driver. The protocol tags are
%%% similar, but the message set is different. 
%%% The protocol only exists internally between edlin and a character
%%% displaying device...
%%% We are *not* really unicode aware yet, we just filter away characters 
%%% beyond the latin1 range. We however handle the unicode binaries...
io_request({window_change, OldTty}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    window_change(Tty, OldTty, Buf);
io_request({put_chars, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    put_chars(bin_to_list(Cs), Buf, Tty);
io_request({put_chars, unicode, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    put_chars(unicode:characters_to_list(Cs,unicode), Buf, Tty);
io_request({put_expand, unicode, Expand, _N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    insert_chars(unicode:characters_to_list("\n"++Expand, unicode), Buf, Tty);
io_request({insert_chars, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    insert_chars(bin_to_list(Cs), Buf, Tty);
io_request({insert_chars, unicode, Cs}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    insert_chars(unicode:characters_to_list(Cs,unicode), Buf, Tty);
io_request({move_rel, N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    move_rel(N, Buf, Tty);
io_request({move_line, N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    move_line(N, Buf, Tty);
io_request({move_combo, L, V, R}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    {ML, Buf1} = move_rel(L, Buf, Tty),
    {MV, Buf2} = move_line(V, Buf1, Tty),
    {MR, Buf3} = move_rel(R, Buf2, Tty),
    {[ML,MV,MR], Buf3};
io_request(new_prompt, _Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
    {[], {[], {[],[]}, [], 0 }};
io_request(delete_line, {_, {_, _}, _, Col}, Tty, _Group) ->
    MoveToBeg = move_cursor(Col, 0, Tty),
    {[MoveToBeg, "\e[J"],
     {[],{[],[]},[],0}};
io_request({redraw_prompt, Pbs, Pbs2, {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA}}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    {ClearLine, Cleared} = io_request(delete_line, Buf, Tty, _Group),
    CL = lists:reverse(Bef,Aft),
    Text = Pbs ++ lists:flatten(lists:join("\n"++Pbs2, lists:reverse(LB)++[CL|LA])),
    Moves = if LA /= [] ->
                    [Last|_] = lists:reverse(LA),
                    {move_combo, -length(Last), -length(LA), length(Bef)};
               true ->
                    {move_rel, -length(Aft)}
            end,
    {T, InsertedText} = io_request({insert_chars, unicode:characters_to_binary(Text)}, Cleared, Tty, _Group),
    {M, Moved} = io_request(Moves, InsertedText, Tty, _Group),
    {[ClearLine, T, M], Moved};
io_request({delete_chars,N}, Buf, Tty, _Group) ->
    delete_chars(N, Buf, Tty);
io_request(clear, Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
    {"\e[H\e[2J", Buf};
io_request(beep, Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
    {[7], Buf};

%% New in R12
io_request({get_geometry,columns},Buf,Tty, _Group) ->
    {ok, Tty#ssh_pty.width, Buf};
io_request({get_geometry,rows},Buf,Tty, _Group) ->
    {ok, Tty#ssh_pty.height, Buf};
io_request({requests,Rs}, Buf, Tty, Group) ->
    io_requests(Rs, Buf, Tty, [], Group);
io_request(tty_geometry, Buf, Tty, Group) ->
    io_requests([{move_rel, 0}, {put_chars, unicode, [10]}],
                Buf, Tty, [], Group);

%% New in 18
io_request({put_chars_sync, Class, Cs, Reply}, Buf, Tty, Group) ->
    %% We handle these asynchronous for now, if we need output guarantees
    %% we have to handle these synchronously
    Group ! {reply, Reply, ok},
    io_request({put_chars, Class, Cs}, Buf, Tty, Group);

io_request(_R, Buf, _Tty, _Group) ->
    {[], Buf}.

io_requests([R|Rs], Buf, Tty, Acc, Group) ->
    {Chars, NewBuf} = io_request(R, Buf, Tty, Group),
    io_requests(Rs, NewBuf, Tty, [Acc|Chars], Group);
io_requests([], Buf, _Tty, Acc, _Group) ->
    {Acc, Buf}.

%%% return commands for cursor navigation, assume everything is ansi
%%% (vt100), add clauses for other terminal types if needed
ansi_tty(N, L) ->
    ["\e[", integer_to_list(N), L].

get_tty_command(up, N, _TerminalType) ->
    ansi_tty(N, $A);
get_tty_command(down, N, _TerminalType) ->
    ansi_tty(N, $B);
get_tty_command(right, N, _TerminalType) ->
    ansi_tty(N, $C);
get_tty_command(left, N, _TerminalType) ->
    ansi_tty(N, $D).


-define(PAD, 10).
-define(TABWIDTH, 8).

%% convert input characters to buffer and to writeout
%% Note that Bef is reversed but Aft is not
%% (this is handy; the head is always next to the cursor)
conv_buf([], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, _Tty) ->
    {{LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, lists:reverse(AccWrite)};
conv_buf([13, 10 | Rest], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, Tty = #ssh_pty{width = W}) ->
    conv_buf(Rest, {[lists:reverse(Bef)|LB], {[], tl2(Aft)}, LA, Col+(W-(Col rem W))}, [10, 13 | AccWrite], Tty);
conv_buf([13 | Rest], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, Tty = #ssh_pty{width = W}) ->
    conv_buf(Rest, {[lists:reverse(Bef)|LB], {[], tl1(Aft)}, LA, Col+(W-(Col rem W))}, [13 | AccWrite], Tty);
conv_buf([10 | Rest],{LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite0, Tty = #ssh_pty{width = W}) ->
    AccWrite =
        case pty_opt(onlcr,Tty) of
            0 -> [10 | AccWrite0];
            1 -> [10,13 | AccWrite0];
            undefined -> [10 | AccWrite0]
        end,
    conv_buf(Rest, {[lists:reverse(Bef)|LB], {[], tl1(Aft)}, LA, Col+(W - (Col rem W))}, AccWrite, Tty);
conv_buf([C | Rest], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}, AccWrite, Tty) ->
    conv_buf(Rest, {LB, {[C|Bef], tl1(Aft)}, LA, Col+1}, [C | AccWrite], Tty).

%%% put characters before the prompt
put_chars(Chars, Buf, Tty) ->
    Dumb = get_dumb(Tty),
    case Buf of
        {[],{[],[]},[],_} -> {_, WriteBuf} = conv_buf(Chars, Buf, [], Tty),
            {WriteBuf, Buf};
        _ when Dumb =:= false ->
            {Delete, DeletedState} = io_request(delete_line, Buf, Tty, []),
            {_, PutBuffer} = conv_buf(Chars, DeletedState, [], Tty),
            {Redraw, _} = io_request(redraw_prompt_pre_deleted, Buf, Tty, []),
            {[Delete, PutBuffer, Redraw], Buf};
        _ ->
            %% When we have a dumb terminal, we get messages via put_chars requests
            %% so state should be empty {[],{[],[]},[],_},
            %% but if we end up here its not, so keep the state
            {_, WriteBuf} = conv_buf(Chars, Buf, [], Tty),
            {WriteBuf, Buf}
    end.

%%% insert character at current position
insert_chars([], Buf, _Tty) ->
    {[], Buf};
insert_chars(Chars, {_LB,{_Bef, Aft},LA, _Col}=Buf, Tty) ->
    {{NewLB, {NewBef, _NewAft}, _NewLA, NewCol}, WriteBuf} = conv_buf(Chars, Buf, [], Tty),
    M = move_cursor(special_at_width(NewCol+length(Aft), Tty), NewCol, Tty),
    {[WriteBuf, Aft | M], {NewLB,{NewBef, Aft},LA, NewCol}}.

%%% delete characters at current position, (backwards if negative argument)
delete_chars(0, {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}, _Tty) ->
    {[], {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}};
delete_chars(N, {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}, Tty) when N > 0 ->
    NewAft = nthtail(N, Aft),
    M = move_cursor(Col + length(NewAft) + N, Col, Tty),
    {[NewAft, lists:duplicate(N, $ ) | M],
     {LB,{Bef, NewAft},LA, Col}};
delete_chars(N, {LB,{Bef, Aft},LA, Col}, Tty) -> % N < 0
    NewBef = nthtail(-N, Bef),
    NewCol = case Col + N of V when V >= 0 -> V; _ -> 0 end,
    M1 = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
    M2 = move_cursor(special_at_width(NewCol+length(Aft)-N, Tty), NewCol, Tty),
    {[M1, Aft, lists:duplicate(-N, $ ) | M2],
     {LB,{NewBef, Aft},LA, NewCol}}.

%%% Window change, redraw the current line (and clear out after it
%%% if current window is wider than previous)
window_change(Tty, OldTty, Buf)
  when OldTty#ssh_pty.width == Tty#ssh_pty.width ->
     %% No line width change
    {[], Buf};
window_change(Tty, OldTty, {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}) ->
    case OldTty#ssh_pty.width - Tty#ssh_pty.width of
        0 ->
            %% No line width change
            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}};

        DeltaW0 when DeltaW0 < 0,
                     Aft == [] ->
            % Line width is decreased, cursor is at end of input
            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}};

        DeltaW0 when DeltaW0 < 0,
                     Aft =/= [] ->
            % Line width is decreased, cursor is not at end of input
            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}};

        DeltaW0 when DeltaW0 > 0 ->
            % Line width is increased
            {[], {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}}
        end.

%% move around in buffer, respecting pad characters
step_over(0, {LB, {Bef, [?PAD |Aft]}, LA, Col}) ->
    {LB, {[?PAD | Bef], Aft}, LA, Col+1};
step_over(0, {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col}) ->
    {LB, {Bef, Aft}, LA, Col};
step_over(N, {LB, {[C | Bef], Aft}, LA, Col}) when N < 0 ->
    N1 = ifelse(C == ?PAD, N, N+1),
    step_over(N1, {LB, {Bef, [C | Aft]}, LA, Col-1});
step_over(N, {LB, {Bef, [C | Aft]}, LA, Col}) when N > 0 ->
    N1 = ifelse(C == ?PAD, N, N-1),
    step_over(N1, {LB, {[C | Bef], Aft}, LA, Col+1}).

%%% an empty line buffer
empty_buf() -> {[], {[], []}, [], 0}.

%%% col and row from position with given width
col(N, W) -> N rem W.
row(N, W) -> N div W.

%%% move relative N characters
move_rel(N, {_LB, {_Bef, _Aft}, _LA, Col}=Buf, Tty) ->
    {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol} = step_over(N, Buf),
    M = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
    {M, {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol}}.

move_line(V, {_LB, {_Bef, _Aft}, _LA, Col}, Tty = #ssh_pty{width=W})
        when V < 0, length(_LB) >= -V ->
    {LinesJumped, [B|NewLB]} = lists:split(-V -1, _LB),
    CL = lists:reverse(_Bef,_Aft),
    NewLA = lists:reverse([CL|LinesJumped], _LA),
    {NewBB, NewAft} = lists:split(min(length(_Bef),length(B)), B),
    NewBef = lists:reverse(NewBB),
    NewCol = Col - length(_Bef) - lists:sum([((length(L)-1) div W)*W + W || L <- [B|LinesJumped]]) + length(NewBB),
    M = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
    {M, {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol}};
move_line(V, {_LB, {_Bef, _Aft}, _LA, Col}, Tty = #ssh_pty{width=W})
        when V > 0, length(_LA) >= V ->
    {LinesJumped, [A|NewLA]} = lists:split(V -1, _LA),
    CL = lists:reverse(_Bef,_Aft),
    NewLB = lists:reverse([CL|LinesJumped],_LB),
    {NewBB, NewAft} = lists:split(min(length(_Bef),length(A)), A),
    NewBef = lists:reverse(NewBB),
    NewCol = Col - length(_Bef) + lists:sum([((length(L)-1) div W)*W + W || L <- [CL|LinesJumped]]) + length(NewBB),
    M = move_cursor(Col, NewCol, Tty),
    {M, {NewLB, {NewBef, NewAft}, NewLA, NewCol}};
move_line(_, Buf, _) ->
    {"", Buf}.
%%% give move command for tty
move_cursor(A, A, _Tty) ->
    [];
move_cursor(From, To, #ssh_pty{width=Width, term=Type}) ->
    Tcol = case col(To, Width) - col(From, Width) of
	       0 -> "";
	       I when I < 0 -> get_tty_command(left, -I, Type);
	       I -> get_tty_command(right, I, Type)
	end,
    Trow = case row(To, Width) - row(From, Width) of
	       0 -> "";
	       J when J < 0 -> get_tty_command(up, -J, Type);
	       J -> get_tty_command(down, J, Type)
	   end,
    [Tcol | Trow].

%%% Caution for line "breaks"
special_at_width(From0, #ssh_pty{width=Width}) when (From0 rem Width) == 0 -> From0 - 1;
special_at_width(From0, _) -> From0.

%% %%% write out characters
%% %%% make sure that there is data to send
%% %%% before calling ssh_connection:send
write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Chars) ->
    write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, ?SSH_EXTENDED_DATA_DEFAULT, Chars).

write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Type, Chars) ->
    case has_chars(Chars) of
        false -> ok;
        true -> ssh_connection:send(ConnectionHandler,
                                    ChannelId,
                                    Type,
                                    Chars)
    end.

has_chars([C|_]) when is_integer(C) -> true;
has_chars([H|T]) when is_list(H) ; is_binary(H) -> has_chars(H) orelse has_chars(T);
has_chars(<<_:8,_/binary>>) -> true;
has_chars(_) -> false.
    

%%% tail, works with empty lists
tl1([_|A]) -> A;
tl1(_) -> [].

%%% second tail
tl2([_,_|A]) -> A;
tl2(_) -> [].

%%% nthtail as in lists, but no badarg if n > the length of list
nthtail(0, A) -> A;
nthtail(N, [_ | A]) when N > 0 -> nthtail(N-1, A);
nthtail(_, _) -> [].

ifelse(Cond, A, B) ->
    case Cond of
	true -> A;
	_ -> B
    end.	    

bin_to_list(B) when is_binary(B) ->
    binary_to_list(B);
bin_to_list(L) when is_list(L) ->
    lists:flatten([bin_to_list(A) || A <- L]);
bin_to_list(I) when is_integer(I) ->
    I.


%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
start_shell(ConnectionHandler, State) ->
    ShellSpawner =
        case State#state.shell of
            Shell when is_function(Shell, 1) ->
                [{user,User}] = ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [user]),
                fun() -> Shell(User) end;
            Shell when is_function(Shell, 2) ->
                ConnectionInfo =
                    ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [peer, user]),
                User = proplists:get_value(user, ConnectionInfo),
                {_, PeerAddr} = proplists:get_value(peer, ConnectionInfo),
                fun() -> Shell(User, PeerAddr) end;
            {_,_,_} = Shell ->
                Shell
        end,
    State#state{group = group:start(self(), ShellSpawner,
                                    [{dumb, get_dumb(State#state.pty)},{expand_below, false},
                                     {echo, get_echo(State#state.pty)}]),
                buf = empty_buf()}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
start_exec_shell(ConnectionHandler, Cmd, State) ->
    ExecShellSpawner =
        case State#state.exec of
            ExecShell when is_function(ExecShell, 1) ->
                fun() -> ExecShell(Cmd) end;
            ExecShell when is_function(ExecShell, 2) ->
                [{user,User}] = ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [user]),
                fun() -> ExecShell(Cmd, User) end;
            ExecShell when is_function(ExecShell, 3) ->
                ConnectionInfo =
                    ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [peer, user]),
                User = proplists:get_value(user, ConnectionInfo),
                {_, PeerAddr} = proplists:get_value(peer, ConnectionInfo),
                fun() -> ExecShell(Cmd, User, PeerAddr) end;
            {M,F,A} ->
                {M, F, A++[Cmd]}
        end,
    State#state{group = group:start(self(), ExecShellSpawner, [{expand_below, false},
                                                               {echo,false}]),
                buf = empty_buf()}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
exec_in_erlang_default_shell(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, WantReply, State) ->
    exec_in_self_group(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, WantReply, State,
      fun() ->
              eval(parse(scan(Cmd)))
      end).


scan(Cmd) ->
    erl_scan:string(Cmd). 

parse({ok, Tokens, _}) ->
    erl_parse:parse_exprs(Tokens);
parse({error, {_,erl_scan,Cause}, _}) ->
    {error, erl_scan:format_error(Cause)}.

eval({ok, Expr_list}) ->
    {value, Value, _NewBindings} = erl_eval:exprs(Expr_list, erl_eval:new_bindings()),
    {ok, Value};
eval({error, {_,erl_parse,Cause}}) ->
    {error, erl_parse:format_error(Cause)};
eval({error,Error}) ->
    {error, Error}.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
exec_direct(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, Cmd, ExecSpec, WantReply, State) ->
    Fun =
        fun() ->
                if
                    is_function(ExecSpec, 1) ->
                        ExecSpec(Cmd);

                    is_function(ExecSpec, 2) ->
                        [{user,User}] = ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [user]),
                        ExecSpec(Cmd, User);

                    is_function(ExecSpec, 3) ->
                        ConnectionInfo =
                            ssh_connection_handler:connection_info(ConnectionHandler, [peer, user]),
                        User = proplists:get_value(user, ConnectionInfo),
                        {_, PeerAddr} = proplists:get_value(peer, ConnectionInfo),
                        ExecSpec(Cmd, User, PeerAddr);

                    true ->
                        {error, "Bad exec fun in server"}
                end
        end,
    exec_in_self_group(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, WantReply, State, Fun).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Help for directing stdin and stdout from and to the channel from/to the client
%%
exec_in_self_group(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, WantReply, State, Fun) ->
    Exec =
        fun() ->
                spawn(
                  fun() ->
                          case try
                                   ssh_connection:reply_request(ConnectionHandler, WantReply, success, ChannelId),
                                   Fun()
                               of
                                   {ok, Result} ->
                                       {ok, Result};
                                   {error, Error} ->
                                       {error, Error};
                                   X ->
                                       {error, "Bad exec fun in server. Invalid return value: "++t2str(X)}
                               catch error:Err ->
                                       {error,Err};
                                     Cls:Exp ->
                                       {error,{Cls,Exp}}
                               end
                          of
                              {ok,Str} ->
                                  write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, t2str(Str));
                              {error, Str} ->
                                  write_chars(ConnectionHandler, ChannelId, 1, "**Error** "++t2str(Str)),
                                  exit({exit_status, ?EXEC_ERROR_STATUS})
                          end
                  end)
        end,
    {ok, State#state{group = group:start(self(), Exec, [{expand_below, false},
                                                        {echo,false}]),
                     buf = empty_buf()}}.
    

t2str(T) -> try io_lib:format("~s",[T])
            catch _:_ -> io_lib:format("~p",[T])
            end.

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
get_dumb(Tty) ->
    try
        Tty#ssh_pty.term =:= "dumb"
    catch
        _:_ -> false
    end.

% Pty can be undefined if the client never sets any pty options before
% starting the shell.
get_echo(Tty) ->
    case pty_opt(echo,Tty) of
        0 -> false;
        1 -> true;
        undefined -> true
    end.

% Group is undefined if the pty options are sent between open and
% shell messages.
set_echo(#state{group = undefined}) ->
    ok;
set_echo(#state{group = Group, pty = Pty}) ->
    Echo = get_echo(Pty),
    Group ! {self(), echo, Echo}.

not_zero(0, B) -> 
    B;
not_zero(A, _) -> 
    A.

%%%----------------------------------------------------------------
pty_opt(Name, Tty) ->
    try
        proplists:get_value(Name, Tty#ssh_pty.modes, undefined)
    catch
        _:_ -> undefined
    end.
